sourceEvidence: src/services/uta-supervisor/url.ts:10-12: resolveUTAUrl trims OPENALICE_UTA_URL and returns any nonempty value unchanged
entries.currentBehavior: A nonempty explicit environment string wins over the port fallback with no URL parsing, scheme/host policy, userinfo rejection, or structured invalid result. The same raw value is later consumed by proxy, health, restart, and test-connection paths.
entries.problem: Malformed or credential-bearing authority can cross the Alice-to-UTA boundary, and different consumers may normalize it differently. A typo is not distinguishable from a deliberately configured endpoint, so transport errors appear late and untyped.
entries.targetModel: Define `parseUtaEndpoint(raw, policy) -> Result<UtaEndpoint, InvalidEndpoint>`. `UtaEndpoint` contains validated scheme/authority/port, normalized base path, and a redacted display form; reject URL userinfo, fragments or query strings when deployment policy disallows them, empty/invalid host, unsupported scheme, control characters, and disallowed authority. Default deployment policy allows the Guardian's loopback HTTP endpoint; any non-loopback/TLS deployment must be explicitly configured rather than inferred.
pureTransitions: parseExplicitUrl(raw) -> Result<UtaEndpoint, InvalidEndpoint>: trim, URL-parse, validate authority/transport, reject credentials and disallowed query/fragment, normalize trailing slash, and preserve valid path prefix
endpointToHealthUrl(endpoint) -> URL: deterministic `/__uta/health` join without re-parsing raw environment text
entries.effectBoundary: Parsing is pure. The resulting endpoint is consumed by HTTP proxy/probe/restart effects; no resolver call performs DNS, fetch, filesystem, or broker access.
entries.durability: No supervisor persistence. Environment/config remains the source of endpoint truth; diagnostics use a redacted endpoint and never persist URL userinfo or secrets.
errors: InvalidEndpoint{field,redactedValue,reason} -> fail closed before any request
UnsupportedTransport{scheme} -> return configuration error; do not silently fall back to local port when explicit URL was supplied
EmbeddedCredentialsRejected{} -> refuse to carry secrets in a URL
preservedBehavior: A trimmed, valid explicit Guardian URL continues to take precedence over OPENALICE_UTA_PORT.
The endpoint can include a validated path prefix if a deployment intentionally uses one.
No URL-based capability is granted; endpoint validity only enables transport attempts.
replacementSteps: Replace string-returning resolveUTAUrl with a Result/refined endpoint resolver and migrate all callsites to handle invalid configuration.
Use one normalized endpoint in main startup, BFF routes, config test-connection, and restart trigger.
Redact endpoint diagnostics and remove raw environment strings from error/log paths.
verificationCases: ' http://127.0.0.1:47333/ ' -> valid endpoint with canonical base and health URL; URL userinfo, query/fragment when disallowed, invalid port, unsupported scheme, or control characters -> InvalidEndpoint.
Explicit malformed URL plus a valid OPENALICE_UTA_PORT -> explicit error, not silent fallback to the port.
Valid endpoint with UTA offline -> endpoint parses successfully, later effect returns typed Unreachable.
entries.contractRationale: Strict URL parsing, canonical joining and credential rejection remain appropriate boundary guarantees. They are schema/configuration composition for the supervisor only; endpoint validity does not imply provider capability or an order effect.

sourceEvidence: src/services/uta-supervisor/url.ts:13-15: resolveUTAUrl trims OPENALICE_UTA_PORT, uses literal 47333 when empty/absent, and interpolates the raw port into http://127.0.0.1:${port}
entries.currentBehavior: An absent or whitespace-only port intentionally selects 47333. Any other trimmed value, including malformed or out-of-range text, is interpolated without numeric parsing or range checks.
entries.problem: The intentional default is indistinguishable from invalid configuration and malformed values are deferred to fetch/URL parsing. A non-port string can also create an endpoint that violates the loopback deployment contract.
entries.targetModel: Add parsePort(raw) -> Result<Port, InvalidPort>, where Port is an integer in 1..65535. Treat absent/trimmed-empty as the explicit DefaultUtaPort=47333; supplied nonempty values must parse canonically and are never silently replaced. Construct UtaEndpoint{scheme:'http',host:'127.0.0.1',port} through the same endpoint type used by explicit URLs.
pureTransitions: resolveLocalEndpoint(env) -> Result<UtaEndpoint, InvalidPort>: choose explicit valid port or 47333 only for missing/empty input
portToEndpoint(port) -> UtaEndpoint: deterministic loopback URL construction with canonical serialization
entries.effectBoundary: Port parsing and URL construction are pure. Only consumers of UtaEndpoint perform HTTP/proxy/restart effects; no port resolver opens a socket.
entries.durability: No persistence owner; port is deployment configuration. Do not write a resolved port into trading journal or process-control flag.
errors: InvalidPort{raw,reason:'non_numeric'|'fractional'|'out_of_range'} -> configuration failure before network I/O
EndpointConstructionFailure{field} -> typed config failure, not fallback
preservedBehavior: Standalone Alice with no port still targets http://127.0.0.1:47333.
Whitespace around a valid port is accepted after the existing trim behavior.
Guardian-provided explicit URL still wins before local port resolution.
replacementSteps: Introduce the Port constructor and make fallback selection explicit in the endpoint resolver.
Migrate Guardian/UTA startup port consumers to the same validated range contract where they currently call Number/raw interpolation.
Have invalid supplied ports fail closed and surface a configuration response rather than attempting a malformed URL.
verificationCases: Missing, empty, or whitespace-only OPENALICE_UTA_PORT -> Port(47333); '1', '65535' -> valid; '0', '65536', '1.5', 'abc' -> InvalidPort.
OPENALICE_UTA_URL valid -> port variable is ignored as before; explicit malformed URL -> InvalidEndpoint rather than local fallback.
A valid port produces exactly loopback HTTP endpoint and is reusable by status, startup, and restart paths.
entries.contractRationale: Port refinement preserves the observed 47333 fallback and rejects supplied invalid values without broadening any provider contract. It is pure deployment configuration and must not be coupled to transaction durability or broker support.

sourceEvidence: src/services/uta-supervisor/url.ts:17-19: isUTADisabled returns a bare boolean from OPENALICE_LITE_MODE or OPENALICE_UTA_DISABLED truthiness
entries.currentBehavior: The function reports only true/false and has no source, mode, lock, configuration, product, or invalid-input information. It is used by trading-mode parsing and the restart guard, while Guardian has a parallel mode parser.
entries.problem: A bare boolean loses the distinction between intentional lite, legacy disable, config mode, nano product disablement, readonly, and temporary endpoint failure. Duplicated consumers can therefore disagree about whether UTA should run or whether only writes should be blocked.
entries.targetModel: Replace `isUTADisabled` with a cycle-free typed legacy-policy parser feeding one `TradingModePolicy` resolver. Use `DisableReason={legacyLiteEnv|legacyUtaDisabledEnv|persistedLite|productNano|autoLite}` and `PolicyState=Enabled{mode:'readonly'|'pro',source,envLocked}|Disabled{reason,source}|InvalidConfiguration`. Keep `CapabilityState` separate so readonly permits reads/process control but blocks venue writes; enabled pro/readonly transport failure is `Unavailable`, never `Disabled`.
pureTransitions: parseLegacyDisableFlags(env) -> Result<DisableSignal, InvalidConfiguration>: preserve accepted true/false spellings and identify source

resolveTradingMode(env,config,product,utaPresence) -> Result<TradingModePolicy, InvalidConfiguration>: explicit mode > legacy disable > persisted mode > auto/product fallback, with one implementation shared by Alice and Guardian
entries.effectBoundary: Policy parsing is pure; composition roots read env/config/product and inject the result into supervisor, proxy, SDK, and Guardian. The supervisor performs no I/O when Disabled/Invalid.
entries.durability: Persisted mode/accounts remain owned by configuration storage and UTA setup; the supervisor does not persist policy or emit trading records.
errors: Disabled{reason,source} -> no UTA restart/probe I/O
InvalidConfiguration{field,raw} -> fail closed and expose correction guidance
ReadOnlyPolicy{mode:'readonly'} -> keep carrier available for reads/process lifecycle while route capability checks reject venue mutation
TransportUnavailable{cause} -> retain Enabled policy and report reachability failure rather than changing mode
preservedBehavior: Both legacy disable environment variables remain recognized.
Explicit trading mode and its env lock continue to be represented, rather than being replaced by endpoint reachability.
Lite, auto-lite, and nano remain intentional no-carrier states; offline pro/readonly is represented as unavailable, not silently converted.
replacementSteps: Delete the boolean helper and centralize mode/legacy/product parsing in one module without introducing a URL↔mode import cycle.
Migrate trading-mode.ts, Guardian runtime mode resolution, main, proxy, SDK, and restart trigger to the policy ADT.
Make all policy branches exhaustive and remove literal 'UTA disabled by OPENALICE_LITE_MODE' fallbacks.
verificationCases: OPENALICE_LITE_MODE=1 or OPENALICE_UTA_DISABLED=true -> Disabled with the correct source and no supervisor effects.
Product=nano or resolved lite/auto-lite -> Disabled even if an endpoint is live; resolved readonly -> process/read operations proceed while venue mutation remains denied by its own policy guard.

Explicit pro plus legacy lite flag follows documented explicit-mode precedence; malformed policy input returns InvalidConfiguration rather than enabling by fallback, and pro/readonly endpoint outage remains Unavailable.
entries.contractRationale: A bare disable boolean cannot express the separate policy and availability states required at this boundary. The target uses a small local policy ADT, while provider capabilities and any controlled effects remain owned by their declarations and execution wrappers.

entries.effectBoundary: The parser is pure and runs before health/file effects. Alice and Guardian receive the same parsed policy; no truthiness parser is allowed at a network, filesystem, or broker boundary.

The four legacy positive spellings remain accepted, case-insensitively.
An explicit valid OPENALICE_TRADING_MODE remains evaluated before legacy disable fallback as in the existing mode parser.

Trim and normalize once at the environment boundary, then make mode/restart/Guardian branches exhaustive over normalized variants.

entries.contractRationale: Fail-closed parsing and source-preserving legacy spellings remain valuable configuration behavior. Centralizing the parser avoids duplicated truthiness rules without imposing one universal provider SDK or adding transaction semantics to process policy.
